brief: A 5.6-second continuous product demonstration proving the visual language for the flagship advertisement: event discovery, fighter comparison, prediction selection and the predictor-rank reward, as one unbroken piece of product motion rather than four screenshots played in order. The interface is real captured Combat Reviews pixels composited onto photographed handsets after the camera move, so type never warps. One dominant direction of motion (upward), two cuts that carry meaning (a screen-position match cut and a cut on the tap), one restrained push-in across the whole sequence, and red used only as an accent.

plates.description: Hero handset, near-frontal, unlit glass on a dark set with a red rim light. Carries the sequence from event discovery through to the rank reward.
Handset held in one hand with the other index finger at the glass. Used only for the tap, and framed so its screen lands where the hero's screen just was.

documents.description: Combat Reviews event discovery — real capture. Shown larger and cropped from the left, because these layouts are left-aligned and a centre crop would keep the whitespace and lose the titles.
Combat Reviews fight card — real full-page capture, natively taller than the screen, so it needs no scaling and scrolls at its own resolution. Carries the corner comparison and the prediction split.
Combat Reviews challenge leaderboard — real capture, prepared like the event list so the two read at the same scale.

states.intent: The list is already moving when the frame opens, and it decelerates into rest. Opening on a settled screen is what makes a product film look like a slideshow; opening mid-scroll says a person is using this.
The list holds and one card takes the accent. The scroll stops before the selection appears so the two readings never compete.

The selected card's own screen pushes up over the list, in the same direction the list was travelling, then settles on the two corners. The push is the transition; there is no dissolve between product states.

The same card keeps scrolling upward to the main event and its prediction split, and the accent lands on the side being backed. One document, one continuous gesture — this is where the sequence earns the word continuous.
Held absolutely still under the finger. The only thing that changes is the control taking the press.
The press releases into a committed state. The cut back to the hero handset lands on this frame, so the confirmation is what the new shot opens on.

The leaderboard pushes up in the same direction everything else has travelled, and the ranked row slides into its resting position under the accent. The reward is the last thing that moves and the last thing that stops.

accents.intent: Red corner, first. Staggering the two corners is what makes it read as a comparison rather than a label.
Blue corner, 0.16s later. The one non-red accent in the cut, because the product itself colours the two corners and overriding that would misrepresent the interface.
The side being backed stays marked through the press and the confirmation — one decision, one mark.
The control taking the touch: a wash and a heavier frame, for the third of a second the finger is down.
Committed. A rule rather than a wash, because the interface underneath still has to be readable.
The row the list has just settled under. It arrives after the scroll stops, so the mark and the movement never fight.

shots.transitionNote: Opens already in motion, on the hero handset, at the shallow end of the push.
Hard cut to the held handset, framed so the screen centre lands where the hero's screen centre just was. The interface does not jump; the hands and the lighting change around it.
Cut on the release of the tap, landing on the confirmed state. The push-in continues from exactly where shot A left it, so the two hero shots read as one move interrupted rather than two shots.
